subject.title: RFC: OpenShell session workers and local inference

question: Should OpenClaw adopt generic worker-local inference and provider-authenticated SSH contracts to support a plugin-gated OpenShell per-session worker provider, including its fixed provider/model limitation?
rationale: This is a new core architectural and security-boundary direction, not a mechanical RFC formatting decision; the repository needs an explicit decision on the durable API and compatibility contract before implementation work should proceed.

options.title: Accept a narrow provider-neutral contract
options.body: Approve the RFC direction only with explicit compatibility, credential-boundary, and worker-protocol invariants, then review the companion implementation against that accepted contract.

options.title: Keep OpenShell sandbox-only
options.body: Decline the new worker and local-inference core contracts and retain the existing plugin sandbox capability without per-session agent-loop placement.

options.title: Request a plugin-only redesign
options.body: Ask for an external integration design that avoids adding generic core inference and transport APIs until a broader worker-provider roadmap is approved.

recommendation.title: Accept a narrow provider-neutral contract
recommendation.body: Approve the RFC direction only with explicit compatibility, credential-boundary, and worker-protocol invariants, then review the companion implementation against that accepted contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Current worker-runtime and plugin API ownership could not be traced because local read-only inspection was blocked.
